(1) the addition of cement, fly ash, or cement kiln dust to weak subgrades improves the strength and stiffness properties of these soils and thus provides a working platform for construction of pavements; (2) the addition of these cementitious additives improves the long-term strength of weak subgrades; (3) the addition of a cementitious additive to weak subgrade soils improves the strength and modulus properties of weak subgrades, and the improvement in strength and modulus properties increases with an increase

(1) the use of cementitious materials can improve the strength and stiffness characteristics of weak subgrade soils, and (2) the design procedures developed in our research can be used to predict the strength and stiffness improvement of weak subgrade materials treated with various types of cementitious additives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation and improvement of the engineering properties of weak subgrade soils through cementitious material stabilization/modification.
evaluating the effectiveness of cementitiously treated soils as subgrade materials for highway pavement.
evaluating the effectiveness of cementitious additives to modify or stabilize weak subgrades to improve their engineering characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cementitious materials can be used to improve the engineering properties (e.g., strength and stiffness) of soils.
cementitiously treated soils are not a viable option for construction of highway pavements in Louisiana.
this research has provided a better understanding of the engineering behavior of cementitiously treated/modified weak subgrade soils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach to evaluate the design parameters and procedures used for the design and construction of cementitious soil stabilization projects.
the cementitious material can be effectively used to treat/stiffen the weak subgrade soils in Louisiana.
the design parameters and procedures that have been developed for cementitiously stabilized soils can be used for cementitiously modified soils.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cementitious material can be successfully used for both soil modification/treatment as well as soil stabilization.
the design of cementitious material treated subgrades can be improved through the use of in-situ cyclic plate load tests.
